prompt:
A close, straight-on photo of the small paper slip printed by a self-service BUS-TERMINAL ticket-and-fare kiosk. A basic add-on fare processor with NO operator precedence tallies the button presses strictly LEFT TO RIGHT, each operator acting at once on the amount currently shown; the divide key does whole-number division that drops any fraction (truncates toward zero). A passenger presses exactly this button sequence, in order:

    7 x 8 + 15 ÷ 2

then presses 'TOTAL'. Work out the final whole number this left-to-right rule produces (NOT standard math order-of-operations) and render the kiosk slip showing that single figure as the FARE TOTAL, printed large in an ordinary plain numeral font (an everyday printed typeface, NOT a seven-segment / segmented-LCD style). Print the button sequence above on a taped strip beside the kiosk. The slip shows only that one final number as the total; no other numbers anywhere except the taped button sequence.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show self-service bus-terminal ticket-and-fare kiosk paper slip photographed straight-on, its fare total in plain printed numerals? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

steps.read_number: This is a photo of a printed ticket-kiosk fare slip. Read the single whole number printed as the FARE TOTAL, ignoring the taped button-sequence strip. Answer with that integer only.

steps.ask: Read the button sequence printed on the taped strip beside the kiosk. Answer with exactly the characters printed there (the digits and operator symbols in order).
Is the large FARE TOTAL numeral printed in an ordinary plain typeface (NOT a seven-segment / segmented-LCD style)? Answer yes or no only.
Does the slip show exactly ONE final total number (with no other numbers on the slip apart from the taped button sequence)? Answer yes or no only.
This kiosk slip prints a sequence of button presses (numbers and operators). Read the FIRST operator symbol that appears between the first two numbers. Answer with just the symbol (x, +, - or /).
